title: Cech vanishing from surjectivity onto unions of cover intersections
statement: Let $Y$ be a topological space, $F$ an abelian sheaf on its open site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $\mathcal U=(U_i)_{i\in I}$ an open covering $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ of an open subset $U\subseteq Y$, indexed by a set $I$. For each finite nonempty $J\subseteq I$ put $U_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}U_j$. Assume that for every family $\mathcal S$ of finite nonempty subsets of $I$, the restriction map $F(U)\longrightarrow F(\bigcup_{J\in\mathcal S}U_J)$ is surjective, including $\mathcal S=\varnothing$. Then $\check H^p(\mathcal U,F)=0$ for every $p>0$. Here Cech cohomology is that of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] on the open site: degree $p\geq0$ is $\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}F(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p})$, with the alternating sum of restriction maps as differential, including tuples with repetitions. No finiteness of $I$, compactness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A36, lemma-vanishing-ravi (statement, lines 1999-2007); intersections indexed by tuples are the same as finite nonempty subsets after removing repetitions.

proof.text: Construct the auxiliary space $P=\{A\subseteq I\mid A\ne\varnothing\}$. For finite nonempty $J\subseteq I$ set $B_J=\{A\in P\mid J\subseteq A\}$. These sets cover $P$, since every $A$ contains some $i$; and $B_J\cap B_K=B_{J\cup K}$, so their arbitrary unions form a topology. Moreover $B_J\subseteq B_K$ iff $K\subseteq J$: necessity follows by testing the point $A=J$, and sufficiency follows from inclusion transitivity. In particular, if an open $W$ contains the point $J$, then $B_J\subseteq W$: choose a basic neighborhood $B_K$ of $J$ inside $W$, so $K\subseteq J$. This also proves that $B_J\subseteq\bigcup_s W_s$ iff $B_J\subseteq W_s$ for some $s$, by testing the point $J$.

For any open $W\subseteq P$ define $T(W)=\bigcup_{J\text{ finite nonempty},\ B_J\subseteq W}U_J$, an open of $Y$ contained in $U$. It is monotone. The inclusion criterion from step 1 gives $T(B_K)=U_K$: the union in its definition ranges exactly over $J\supseteq K$, and contains the term $J=K$. Also $T(\varnothing)=\varnothing$ because $B_J$ contains $J$, and $T(P)=U$ because the singleton terms are $U_i$ and all other terms lie in $U$. These identities remain valid when $I$ is empty: then $P=U=\varnothing$.

The functor $T$ preserves arbitrary unions: the last criterion of step 1 says that a finite nonempty $J$ contributes to $T(\bigcup_s W_s)$ exactly when it contributes to some $T(W_s)$. It preserves binary intersections as well. Monotonicity gives $T(W\cap Z)\subseteq T(W)\cap T(Z)$. Conversely a point in the latter lies in $U_J\cap U_K=U_{J\cup K}$ with $B_J\subseteq W$ and $B_K\subseteq Z$; but $B_{J\cup K}=B_J\cap B_K\subseteq W\cap Z$, giving the other inclusion. Consequently $T$ sends an open covering $W=\bigcup_s W_s$ to the covering $T(W)=\bigcup_s T(W_s)$, and sends $W_s\cap Z$ to $T(W_s)\cap T(Z)$ for every $Z\subseteq W$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf] to $T:\operatorname{Open}(P)\to\operatorname{Open}(Y)$ and $F$. Both sites are small in a universe containing the underlying sets $I,Y$ and their power sets, their arrows are inclusions and coverings are open families. Step 3 verifies both hypotheses of that lemma: image families cover and pullbacks along covering inclusions (intersections) are preserved. Thus $G(W)=F(T(W))$, with restriction maps inherited from $F$, is an abelian sheaf on $P$. No continuous map of underlying topological spaces is asserted or needed.

proof.text: For opens $Z\subseteq W\subseteq P$ and $s\in G(Z)=F(T(Z))$, the hypothesis of the item applied to the family of all finite nonempty $J$ with $B_J\subseteq Z$ gives $t\in F(U)$ restricting to $s$ on $T(Z)$. Restrict $t$ to $T(W)$; this is an element of $G(W)$ restricting to $s$, by functoriality of $F$ and $T(Z)\subseteq T(W)\subseteq U$. Hence every restriction of $G$ is surjective, so $G$ is flasque by [def-sc-zariski-flasque]. This uses the empty-family hypothesis when $Z=\varnothing$.

The family $\mathcal B=(B_{\{i\}})_{i\in I}$ covers $P$. For any tuple $(i_0,\ldots,i_p)$, let $J=\{i_0,\ldots,i_p\}$. Then $\bigcap_k B_{\{i_k\}}=B_J$, $T(B_J)=U_J=\bigcap_k U_{i_k}$, so $G(\bigcap_k B_{\{i_k\}})=F(\bigcap_k U_{i_k})$. For each omitted entry, the restriction between these groups is exactly the restriction of $F$ between the corresponding intersections, since $G$ was defined by precomposition with $T$. Therefore the identity on every tuple component identifies the two products and commutes term by term with each summand $(-1)^k$ in the differential of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. It gives an isomorphism of cochain complexes $\check C^\bullet(\mathcal B,G)\cong\check C^\bullet(\mathcal U,F)$, including tuples with repetitions.

Apply [lem-sfb-flasque-open-cover-cech-acyclic] to the topological space $P$, the abelian sheaf $G$ of step 4, its flasqueness from step 5, and the set-indexed open cover $\mathcal B$ of step 6. It gives $\check H^p(\mathcal B,G)=0$ for $p>0$. The cochain isomorphism in step 6 identifies kernels and images of the differentials, hence identifies these groups with $\check H^p(\mathcal U,F)$, proving the assertion.
